newsitem.title: NORWAY: Esso signs deal for North Sea Jotun oilfield.
newsitem.headline: Esso signs deal for North Sea Jotun oilfield.

text.p: Esso Norge AS said on Wednesday it had signed a 300 million crown deal with Haliburton AS for the engineering, procurement, installation and commissioning for the tie-back and pipeline systems of the Jotun oilfield in the North Sea.

Jotun will be developed via a floating production/storage/offloading vessel and a wellhead platform. Daily production capacity will be around 90,000 barrels a day of crude with start up planned for 1999.
Esso said the plans were dependent upon upon government approval of the project.
The Jotun field is located in blocks 25/8 and 25/7, about 200 km west of Stavanger on the west coast of Norway and 29 km north of Esso's Balder field.
The field comprises three separate structures -- Elli, Tau West and Elli South -- which will be developed as one production unit.
Total reserves are estimated at about 200 million barrels of oil equivalent.

Partners in block 25/8 are Esso as operator and Enterprise Oil Norge with 50 percent each. Partners in block 25/7 are Norske Conoco with 37.5 percent, Amerada Hess Norge with 12.5 percent and Den norske stats oljeselskap AS with 50 percent.
